youtube_video_title: Novak Djokovic vs Jannik Sinner - FULL Semifinal Highlights | Roland Garros 2025
comment_text:
Couple of observations
1) I was surprised with the power coming off Novak's racket. We're always told SInner hits the ball harder than anyone else but I didn't see that much of a difference
2) SInner didn't fully exploit the advantage he created in the rallies, by going too often in the direction Novak was expecting. He's still a little too predictable with the placement of his shots
3) Their styles were more similar in their match-up than usual. If anything, it's Djokovic who was more aggressive, knowing he couldn't outlast his opponent
4) And age was really the key here. Sinner's muscles are reacting a tad faster and he will endure longer too.
5) Sinner knew Djokovic would try shortening the rallies and was prepared for drop shots, standing close enough to the baseline. Djokovic has adopted the drop shot late in his career and although he's very good at it, he still has difficulty creating them off the power of SInner's incoming shots.
6) Sinner must be the strongest in the world when under pressure by Djokovic. He's totally unphased by a break point, or a break. He does what Djokovic does: hold, or rebreak.
